about: Touched-path to test-suite map, read by `botq test-map`. First matching rule wins. `tests: []` means consciously untested and carries its why. Commands run from the repo root; lint with `botq test-map --check`.

rules.why: editing the map re-lints its own completeness
visual proof assets are inspected at their native dimensions

tests: nix-shell --run 'shellcheck art/symbols/gen.sh art/overlay/*.sh && art/symbols/gen.sh && art/overlay/gen.sh -c && cargo test every_symbol_letter_matches_its_binding_and_shift_state && git diff --exit-code -- art/symbols/*.png proofs/tape-case-73.png art/overlay/manual.png'
rules.why: one vector source regenerates every symbol and its shipped-size proof; the manual composites those exact symbols over its reusable page

the machine textures are painted by ziral --gen through paint.sh, their prompts written and their candidates judged through ask.sh; the tests check the shipped scaffolds, prompts, kept candidates, maps and keys against the manifest
the art scripts drive the image tool and the shot renderer; shellcheck is the one static check they have
art direction documents and raster assets; the scripts among them have their own rule above
running the web build is the only thing that compiles the wasm module and checks the wasm-bindgen pin
GitHub is the only runner; the push that lands a workflow is the run that checks it
a parse catches syntax; a build inside the shell catches a missing package
a shader only compiles when a scene is drawn; the proof shot draws lit machines at two turns and fails on a shader error
one crate, one suite; two test threads because the box hangs cargo test under contention
